chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of his companions from Aban from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala' from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) named Hasan and Husayn (peace be upon them) on their seventh day, and performed the 'Aqeeqa for them, a sheep for each, and they sent a leg of a sheep to the midwife, and he ate from the rest, and gifted to the neighbors. And Fatima (peace be upon her) shaved their heads and gave silver in charity equal to the weight of their hair.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals for newborns in Shia Islam according to the Prophet's practice?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the Sunnah of the Prophet (SAW) and Fatima (AS) in performing Aqeeqa for the grandsons, highlighting the communal aspect of charity through sharing meat with neighbors and the midwife. It further emphasizes the virtue of generosity by linking the ritual of shaving the head to a specific charitable act of giving silver equal to the weight of the hair, a practice deeply rooted in Shia tradition as a sign of gratitude and blessing.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from one of his companions, from Aban, from Yahya Bin Abu Al A’ala,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww named Hassanasws and Husaynasws on both theirasws seventh day, and performed Aqeeqa for both of them, a ram, a ram, and sent with a leg (of the slaughtered ram) to the mid-wife, and awaited with other than it. So hesaww ate from it, and gifted to the neighbours. And Syeda Fatimaasws shaved off both theirasws heads, and gave silver in charity by the weight of both theirasws hairs’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from certain persons of his people from Aban from Yahya ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, named al-Hassan and al-Husayn, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, on the seventh day from their birth, offered a sheep for ‘Aqiqah, one leg of the sheep was sent to al-Qabilah (the special nurse) and the rest was kept. They ate thereof and gave as a gift to neighbors. Fatimah, ‘Alayha al-Salam, shaved their heads and gave in charity silver by the weight of the hairs.”’
